notes.meaning: Snow during high summer and rain during harvest time are abnormal weather events that ruin ripe crops. In the same way, giving praise, respect, or high position to a foolish person is unnatural and harmful. When foolish people are honored, they become more arrogant and use their power to hurt others.

A small sparrow flutters about and a swallow darts through the air without landing on anyone. An undeserved curse is just like that bird, because words spoken in malice against an innocent person have no power to cause harm. God protects the innocent, so unfair insults and curses simply vanish in the air.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Douay-Rheims translation follows an ancient variant reading, stating that an undeserved curse will indeed fall upon someone.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some popular teachers treat this verse as a spiritual law of cause and effect, saying every curse has an underlying cause that must be uncovered and removed.

notes.meaning: Drivers use a whip to spur a horse and a bridle to steer an unruly donkey. In the same way, a stubborn fool refuses to listen to reason and must be dealt with through physical discipline and sharp consequences. Painful correction is often the only thing that will restrain a careless person from doing wrong.

Arguing with a fool by copying his angry tone, silly boasting, or insulting words is a serious mistake. Stooping down to match his bad behavior only drags a person down to his level. Wise people keep their self-control and refuse to join in foolish shouting matches.

There are times when a fool's false claims must be answered directly and firmly. Rebuking his error with clear truth exposes how silly his thinking really is. Giving a firm answer prevents the fool from boasting that his argument was unanswerable.

Hiring a foolish person to carry an important message is like cutting off your own feet. The sender ruins his own project and ends up receiving a flood of trouble and damage instead of good news. Relying on an untrustworthy person guarantees failure and brings public embarrassment.

A wise proverb sounds awkward and useless in the mouth of a fool, just like lame legs dangling helplessly from a disabled man. A person who lives an ungodly life cannot practice the wisdom he tries to preach. When a foolish man speaks holy words, his hypocritical lifestyle makes his sayings look ridiculous.

Tying a stone firmly into a sling ruins the weapon, because the stone cannot fly out to reach its target. Conferring dignity, titles, or public honor on a fool is completely wasted in the very same way. A foolish person cannot carry honor well and may end up hurting those who gave it to him.

A drunken man who grabs a sharp thorn branch waves it about carelessly and injures both himself and others. A fool does the exact same kind of damage when he tries to use a wise proverb or quote holy words. Because he lacks good sense, he misapplies the truth and ends up hurting the people around him.

Hiring a foolish person or a random stranger to complete a serious task is reckless and destructive. It causes as much random injury to everyone nearby as an archer who fires arrows blindly into a crowd. Employers who put incompetent or wicked people in charge bring misery to those around them.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Douay-Rheims translation understands the Hebrew differently, rendering it as a statement that judgment decides legal causes and putting a fool to silence stops anger.

notes.meaning: A dog naturally returns to eat the very vomit that made it sick. In the same repulsive way, an unrepentant fool repeats his past sins over and over again. Although his wrong choices brought him misery before, he quickly forgets the pain and dives right back into evil.

A person who is proud and completely convinced of his own wisdom is in grave spiritual danger. There is actually more hope for an ordinary, uneducated fool to learn the truth than for a self-righteous man. Pride blinds people to their own faults and keeps them from seeking God's guidance.

A lazy man invents ridiculous excuses to keep from going outside to do his job. He pretends that a fierce, hungry lion is stalking the public streets and squares. People often dream up imaginary dangers just to justify neglecting their everyday duties.

A heavy door swings back and forth on its hinges all day without ever leaving the doorway. In that exact way, a lazy person turns over and over in bed without ever getting up to do useful work. He makes lots of small motions, but he makes zero real progress in life.

The slacker drops his hand into the bowl of food, but he feels too exhausted to lift it back to his mouth. This humorous exaggeration shows how ridiculous and self-defeating extreme laziness really is. People who refuse to do their duty often make excuses that ordinary tasks are impossible burdens.

The lazy man convinces himself that he is wiser than seven thoughtful, reasonable advisers. Because he avoids the discipline of hard work, he never tests his ideas and never sees his own ignorance. His smug self-satisfaction makes him impossible to teach or correct.

Jumping into someone else's argument as you walk by is just like grabbing a stray dog by the ears. It is difficult to keep holding on, and letting go will only invite an angry bite. Interfering in disputes that are none of your business brings unnecessary danger upon yourself.

A man who lies to his neighbor and then excuses his cruelty by saying he was only joking acts like a madman who shoots fire and lethal arrows into a crowd. Reckless lies and cruel deceit cause real wounds that an excuse cannot heal. Trust and friendship are too precious to be destroyed for the sake of cheap laughs.

A fire quickly dies and turns to cold ash when no one puts more wood onto the pile. In the exact same way, a bitter feud dies down when there is no gossip or talebearer around to repeat secrets. Stopping the spread of slander brings immediate peace to troubled relationships.

Adding charcoal keeps glowing embers hot, and throwing wood onto a fire makes the flames roar. In the same way, an argumentative person naturally fuels anger and starts fights wherever he goes. Peace can only thrive when people refuse to stir up petty conflicts.

Whispered words of gossip are like sweet, tasty treats that people eagerly swallow down. Once heard, these damaging stories sink deep into a person's inner thoughts and quietly shape their opinions. Listening to slander causes deep wounds to friendship and community harmony.

A thin layer of silver glaze can make a cheap, fragile clay pot look valuable and shiny. In the very same way, smooth, affectionate words often hide a rotten, deceitful heart beneath the surface. Wise people look past superficial charm to discern a person's real character.

A hateful person often disguises his true feelings behind polite words and warm greetings. On the outside he pretends to be friendly, while on the inside he stores up deceitful plots to harm others. Malice that hides under pleasant speech is especially dangerous because it catches people off guard.

When a known deceiver speaks kindly and graciously, do not trust what he says. His sweet-sounding words hide a heart completely filled with evil plans and foul motives. Being cautious and guarded protects innocent people from being taken in by fake friendliness.

A deceptive enemy may succeed in hiding his hatred for a season behind smiles and pretend love. In the end, however, God will bring his secret malice to light and expose him before the whole community. Hypocrisy cannot stay hidden forever, and shame eventually catches up to the liar.

A person who digs a deep trap to catch someone else will end up tumbling into it himself. Likewise, the heavy stone rolled uphill to crush an enemy will roll right back upon the plotter. God's moral justice ensures that the harm people design for others will ultimately destroy them instead.

A lying tongue naturally hates the very people it injures with slander and false accusations. At the same time, smooth flattery works hidden destruction by puffing up a listener with foolish pride. False praise is often more dangerous than an open attack because it leads victims into ruin.
